content.content:
1	# Global Header, Mega Menu, Search & Contentful Nav (SFCC-52, SFCC-746, SFCC-747, SFCC-96, SFCC-97, SFCC-93)
2	
3	## ⏸ Resume point (as of 2026-08-30, later still — committed and pushed (`0b1e706`); this is the current head of the branch)
4	
5	**Committed and pushed** — `0b1e706` on `feature/sfcc-52-global-header`, 27 files (+1292/-467),
6	no local CodeRabbit review this round (Tim's explicit instruction). Covers everything in this
7	entry plus the two entries below it (nav underline grow/reverse/concurrency, mega-menu
8	open/switch/close choreography, the flash-fix and transition-stall-fix bugs, and the comment
9	cleanup pass).
10	
11	**Deliberately excluded from the commit** — both predate this session, unrelated to the motion
12	work:
13	- `overrides/app/constants/index.ts` — a stray `TODO: Review this file and remove any constants
14	  that are not used.` comment nobody in this conversation added, appended to the base SFCC
15	  license header. Unexplained; flagged to Tim, not investigated further.
16	- `translations/en-{GB,US}.json` + their `overrides/app/static/translations/compiled/` copies —
17	  the same pre-existing drift that was already sitting uncommitted at the very start of this
18	  session (see this memory file's original loose-end note); still untouched.
19	
20	Both remain in the working tree, uncommitted, as of this session's end — a fresh session should
21	either investigate/commit them separately or continue leaving them alone, but should not silently
22	fold them into unrelated future commits without checking first.
23	
24	### What's left
25	
26	- Everything below this entry (footer's fade underline untouched by design, provisional
27	  duration/easing values pending final design confirmation, no mobile motion spec yet, the
28	  `useHeaderNav.ts` locale bug, L2 four-axis review for Clothing/Accessories/New, the dead
29	  `listMenuTriggerLink` styles in `list-menu.css.ts`) is still open — this commit didn't close
30	  any of those, it only shipped the motion work itself.
31	- Get a human non-author Tier 2 reviewer on PR #65 — still the standing blocker, unrelated to
32	  this work (`mergeStateStatus: BLOCKED` / `reviewDecision` needs a fresh review).
33	
34	---
35	
36	## ⏸ Resume point (as of 2026-08-30, later still — trigger-underline concurrency fix + comment cleanup pass; committed above)
37	
38	**Tim confirmed the retract-direction fix, then flagged one more thing**: switching L1 items
39	showed the old trigger's underline staying fully visible until the whole content fade-out
40	finished, instead of both triggers' underlines animating at the same time. Root cause: the
41	underline's `active` state was driven by the same `isOpen` value used for Popover pre-positioning
42	(true for both outgoing and incoming item throughout a switch, by design — see the flash-fix
43	entry below), so the outgoing trigger never started retracting until `activeItemId` actually
44	swapped. Fixed by decoupling a third concept: `isTriggerActive` = "the most recently *hovered*
45	item" (`pendingItemId ?? activeItemId` in `list-menu.tsx`), which changes the instant a new item
46	is hovered, independent of the content-fade timing. Renamed `ListMenuTrigger`'s prop from the
47	misleading `isOpen` to `isActive` accordingly. Verified via the same `getComputedStyle` sampling
48	technique: both underlines' `scaleX` values now move concurrently in the same frame, one
49	retracting while the other grows.
50	
51	**Then, separately, Tim asked for a comment cleanup pass** across `drawer-menu/`, `list-menu/`,
52	`ui-kits/atoms/zimmNavItem/`, and `useMegaMenuMotion.ts` — trimmed verbose narrative comments
53	(dated "confirmed via X"/"developer's explicit report" framing, multi-sentence backstory) down to
54	the pertinent non-obvious "why" only, across all 13 production source files in those folders
55	(~1721 -> ~1487 lines). Noted for the record: production builds already strip comments via
56	minification, so this doesn't actually change shipped bundle size — the value is maintainability,
57	not runtime performance, which Tim's request had framed it as.
58	
59	`npx tsc --noEmit`, full Vitest (517 tests, unchanged), `npm run audit:tokens` (all `audit-allow`
60	exceptions survived the trim), and a full `test-storybook` run (140 tests) all clean.
61	
62	### Remaining / open, going into next
63	
64	- **Not committed or pushed.**
65	- Everything else from the entries below still applies.
66	
67	---
68	
69	## ⏸ Resume point (as of 2026-08-30, later same day — underline retract-direction fix on top of the entry below; committed in `0b1e706` above)
70	
71	**Tim confirmed the mega-menu open/switch/close choreography and the underline's grow direction
72	are both correct**, but flagged the underline's *retract* (blur) direction as still wrong: it
73	visually animated left-to-right toward 0, same as growth, when it should retract right-to-left.
74	
75	**Root cause was a perceptual bug in the original fix's reasoning, not a mechanical one.** The
76	first version flipped `transform-origin` from `left` (hover) back to `right` (rest) on blur,
77	reasoning that the *anchored* edge should mirror the grow direction. But a viewer perceives an
78	animation's direction by which edge is *moving*, not which edge is fixed — with origin `right`,
79	the moving edge (the left edge, retreating toward the fixed right anchor) travels left-to-right,
80	exactly the wrong-but-observed behavior. **Fix**: `transform-origin` now stays fixed at `left` in
81	both states — never flips. This makes blur a true reverse of hover: the moving (right) edge
82	retreats right-to-left back to the fixed left anchor, matching the request exactly. Simpler than
83	the original implementation too — one origin value instead of two states to keep in sync.
84	
85	Verified via the same precise `getComputedStyle` sampling technique as the original underline
86	work (not just visual screenshots): `transformOrigin` confirmed fixed at `"0px 0.5px"` (left)
87	throughout the retract, `scaleX` smoothly decreasing 1→0. `npx tsc --noEmit`, full Vitest (516
88	tests, unchanged — `ZimmNavItem` has no dedicated test file, per components.md's exemption for a
89	pure prop-interpolation atom; Storybook is its coverage layer), `npm run audit:tokens`, and a
90	full `test-storybook` run (140 tests) all clean.
91	
92	### Remaining / open, going into next
93	
94	- **Not committed or pushed.**
95	- Everything else from the entry below still applies (provisional duration/easing values, no
96	  mobile motion spec yet, `useHeaderNav.ts` locale bug, L2 four-axis review, dead
97	  `listMenuTriggerLink` styles).
98	
99	---
100	
101	## ⏸ Resume point (as of 2026-08-30 — Motion phase 1: desktop/tablet nav underline + mega-menu open/switch/close choreography; committed in `0b1e706` above)
102	
103	**New phase of work, following the DSI revert.** Tim gave a full verbal motion spec for
104	desktop/tablet only (no mobile spec yet): (1) nav-link underline grows left-to-right on hover,
105	ease-in, and reverses direction on blur — all menus in the navigation; (2) mega-menu opens with a
106	top-to-bottom height reveal, ease-in, then content fades in; switching between L1 items fades the
107	old content out then the new content in with **no height change**; closing fades content out then
108	collapses the reveal in reverse. Plan was presented and confirmed before implementing (Coding Task
109	Workflow step 2), including one `AskUserQuestion` on the switch-height question (confirmed: height
110	must never move on switch) and one on underline scope (confirmed: nav contexts only, not footer).
111	
112	### What shipped
113	
114	**1. Nav-link underline** — added `growUnderline` prop to `ZimmNavItem`
115	(`ui-kits/atoms/zimmNavItem/`), opt-in via a new `GROW_UNDERLINE_SX` style block
116	(`zimmNavItem.css.ts`) that replaces the shared atom's default fade (`border-bottom-color`
117	transition) with a `::after` pseudo-element that scales in width instead (a border can't itself be
118	grown via transform). Wired at desktop/tablet nav call sites only — `list-menu-trigger.tsx`,
119	`list-menu.tsx`'s direct-link items, `megaMenuContent/index.tsx`'s leaf links — **not** the mobile
120	drawer (no motion spec yet) and **not** the footer (Tim's explicit scope call; footer keeps its
121	existing fade). Verified via precise `getComputedStyle` sampling in a real browser (not just
122	visual screenshots) that the transform genuinely interpolates 0→1 with `ease-in`'s characteristic
123	slow-start/fast-finish curve on hover-in, and correctly reverses (shrinks toward a right-anchored
124	origin, not just fading) on hover-out.
125	
126	**Real, unrelated discovery along the way**: the *dead* `listMenuTriggerLink`/`_after` styles in
127	`list-menu.css.ts` (edited in an earlier round of this same motion work, before this session
128	realized they were unused) are not what actually renders — `ListMenuTrigger` renders `ZimmNavItem`,
129	which has its own separate underline mechanism in `zimmNavItem.css.ts`. That earlier edit is
130	harmless dead code, left as-is (not the current session's job to clean up, but worth knowing next
131	time nav-underline work touches this area).
132	
133	**2. Mega-menu open/switch/close** — new `overrides/app/hooks/useMegaMenuMotion.ts`, a phase
134	state machine (`closed → expanding → contentIn → open → contentOut → collapsing → closed`,
135	switch = `contentOut` with a `pendingItemId` instead of an instant swap) replacing `list-menu.tsx`'s
136	old raw `openItemId` state. `list-menu-popover.tsx` renders the height reveal via the CSS
137	`grid-template-rows: 0fr↔1fr` technique (animates to/from an unknown height with no JS
138	measurement — works identically for desktop's fixed promo image and tablet's fluid one) and the
139	content fade via plain `opacity`, both driven by the shared phase, with `onTransitionEnd` wired
140	back to the hook's `on*Complete` actions.
141	
142	**Two real, non-obvious bugs found and fixed via direct browser/DOM verification, not
143	assumption** (both were things a purely-visual check would have missed or misattributed):
144	
145	- **A flash-of-page-content gap during a switch.** Confirmed live: switching from one open L1 item
146	  to another showed a frame or two of the page's own hero content through the header before the
147	  new panel's white background caught up. Root cause: swapping *which* item's Popover is
148	  Chakra-`isOpen` happens in one commit, and the newly-opened one's `PopoverContent` needs at
149	  least one paint to mount/position (`variant="fullWidth"`'s `popper` styling still runs through
150	  Chakra's normal open-transition machinery even though the visual position is CSS-forced to

**Committed and pushed** — `0b1e706` on `feature/sfcc-52-global-header`, 27 files (+1292/-467),

cleanup pass).

**Deliberately excluded from the commit** — both predate this session, unrelated to the motion
work:
- `overrides/app/constants/index.ts` — a stray `TODO: Review this file and remove any constants

Both remain in the working tree, uncommitted, as of this session's end — a fresh session should
either investigate/commit them separately or continue leaving them alone, but should not silently
fold them into unrelated future commits without checking first.

### What's left

- Everything below this entry (footer's fade underline untouched by design, provisional
  duration/easing values pending final design confirmation, no mobile motion spec yet, the
  `useHeaderNav.ts` locale bug, L2 four-axis review for Clothing/Accessories/New, the dead
  `listMenuTriggerLink` styles in `list-menu.css.ts`) is still open — this commit didn't close

## ⏸ Resume point (as of 2026-08-30, later still — trigger-underline concurrency fix + comment cleanup pass; committed above)

**Tim confirmed the retract-direction fix, then flagged one more thing**: switching L1 items
showed the old trigger's underline staying fully visible until the whole content fade-out
finished, instead of both triggers' underlines animating at the same time. Root cause: the
underline's `active` state was driven by the same `isOpen` value used for Popover pre-positioning
(true for both outgoing and incoming item throughout a switch, by design — see the flash-fix
entry below), so the outgoing trigger never started retracting until `activeItemId` actually
swapped. Fixed by decoupling a third concept: `isTriggerActive` = "the most recently *hovered*
item" (`pendingItemId ?? activeItemId` in `list-menu.tsx`), which changes the instant a new item
is hovered, independent of the content-fade timing. Renamed `ListMenuTrigger`'s prop from the
misleading `isOpen` to `isActive` accordingly. Verified via the same `getComputedStyle` sampling
technique: both underlines' `scaleX` values now move concurrently in the same frame, one
retracting while the other grows.

**Then, separately, Tim asked for a comment cleanup pass** across `drawer-menu/`, `list-menu/`,
`ui-kits/atoms/zimmNavItem/`, and `useMegaMenuMotion.ts` — trimmed verbose narrative comments
(dated "confirmed via X"/"developer's explicit report" framing, multi-sentence backstory) down to
the pertinent non-obvious "why" only, across all 13 production source files in those folders
(~1721 -> ~1487 lines). Noted for the record: production builds already strip comments via
minification, so this doesn't actually change shipped bundle size — the value is maintainability,
not runtime performance, which Tim's request had framed it as.

`npx tsc --noEmit`, full Vitest (517 tests, unchanged), `npm run audit:tokens` (all `audit-allow`
exceptions survived the trim), and a full `test-storybook` run (140 tests) all clean.

### Remaining / open, going into next

- **Not committed or pushed.**
- Everything else from the entries below still applies.

## ⏸ Resume point (as of 2026-08-30, later same day — underline retract-direction fix on top of the entry below; committed in `0b1e706` above)

**Tim confirmed the mega-menu open/switch/close choreography and the underline's grow direction
are both correct**, but flagged the underline's *retract* (blur) direction as still wrong: it
visually animated left-to-right toward 0, same as growth, when it should retract right-to-left.

**Root cause was a perceptual bug in the original fix's reasoning, not a mechanical one.** The
first version flipped `transform-origin` from `left` (hover) back to `right` (rest) on blur,
reasoning that the *anchored* edge should mirror the grow direction. But a viewer perceives an
animation's direction by which edge is *moving*, not which edge is fixed — with origin `right`,
the moving edge (the left edge, retreating toward the fixed right anchor) travels left-to-right,
exactly the wrong-but-observed behavior. **Fix**: `transform-origin` now stays fixed at `left` in
both states — never flips. This makes blur a true reverse of hover: the moving (right) edge
retreats right-to-left back to the fixed left anchor, matching the request exactly. Simpler than
the original implementation too — one origin value instead of two states to keep in sync.

Verified via the same precise `getComputedStyle` sampling technique as the original underline
work (not just visual screenshots): `transformOrigin` confirmed fixed at `"0px 0.5px"` (left)
throughout the retract, `scaleX` smoothly decreasing 1→0. `npx tsc --noEmit`, full Vitest (516
tests, unchanged — `ZimmNavItem` has no dedicated test file, per components.md's exemption for a
pure prop-interpolation atom; Storybook is its coverage layer), `npm run audit:tokens`, and a
full `test-storybook` run (140 tests) all clean.

### Remaining / open, going into next

- **Not committed or pushed.**
- Everything else from the entry below still applies (provisional duration/easing values, no
  mobile motion spec yet, `useHeaderNav.ts` locale bug, L2 four-axis review, dead
  `listMenuTriggerLink` styles).

## ⏸ Resume point (as of 2026-08-30 — Motion phase 1: desktop/tablet nav underline + mega-menu open/switch/close choreography; committed in `0b1e706` above)

**New phase of work, following the DSI revert.** Tim gave a full verbal motion spec for
desktop/tablet only (no mobile spec yet): (1) nav-link underline grows left-to-right on hover,
ease-in, and reverses direction on blur — all menus in the navigation; (2) mega-menu opens with a
top-to-bottom height reveal, ease-in, then content fades in; switching between L1 items fades the
old content out then the new content in with **no height change**; closing fades content out then
collapses the reveal in reverse. Plan was presented and confirmed before implementing (Coding Task
Workflow step 2), including one `AskUserQuestion` on the switch-height question (confirmed: height
must never move on switch) and one on underline scope (confirmed: nav contexts only, not footer).

### What shipped

**1. Nav-link underline** — added `growUnderline` prop to `ZimmNavItem`
(`ui-kits/atoms/zimmNavItem/`), opt-in via a new `GROW_UNDERLINE_SX` style block
(`zimmNavItem.css.ts`) that replaces the shared atom's default fade (`border-bottom-color`
transition) with a `::after` pseudo-element that scales in width instead (a border can't itself be
grown via transform). Wired at desktop/tablet nav call sites only — `list-menu-trigger.tsx`,
`list-menu.tsx`'s direct-link items, `megaMenuContent/index.tsx`'s leaf links — **not** the mobile
drawer (no motion spec yet) and **not** the footer (Tim's explicit scope call; footer keeps its
existing fade). Verified via precise `getComputedStyle` sampling in a real browser (not just
visual screenshots) that the transform genuinely interpolates 0→1 with `ease-in`'s characteristic
slow-start/fast-finish curve on hover-in, and correctly reverses (shrinks toward a right-anchored
origin, not just fading) on hover-out.

**Real, unrelated discovery along the way**: the *dead* `listMenuTriggerLink`/`_after` styles in
`list-menu.css.ts` (edited in an earlier round of this same motion work, before this session
realized they were unused) are not what actually renders — `ListMenuTrigger` renders `ZimmNavItem`,
which has its own separate underline mechanism in `zimmNavItem.css.ts`. That earlier edit is
harmless dead code, left as-is (not the current session's job to clean up, but worth knowing next
time nav-underline work touches this area).

**2. Mega-menu open/switch/close** — new `overrides/app/hooks/useMegaMenuMotion.ts`, a phase
state machine (`closed → expanding → contentIn → open → contentOut → collapsing → closed`,
switch = `contentOut` with a `pendingItemId` instead of an instant swap) replacing `list-menu.tsx`'s
old raw `openItemId` state. `list-menu-popover.tsx` renders the height reveal via the CSS
`grid-template-rows: 0fr↔1fr` technique (animates to/from an unknown height with no JS
measurement — works identically for desktop's fixed promo image and tablet's fluid one) and the
content fade via plain `opacity`, both driven by the shared phase, with `onTransitionEnd` wired
back to the hook's `on*Complete` actions.

**Two real, non-obvious bugs found and fixed via direct browser/DOM verification, not
assumption** (both were things a purely-visual check would have missed or misattributed):

- **A flash-of-page-content gap during a switch.** Confirmed live: switching from one open L1 item
  to another showed a frame or two of the page's own hero content through the header before the
  new panel's white background caught up. Root cause: swapping *which* item's Popover is
  Chakra-`isOpen` happens in one commit, and the newly-opened one's `PopoverContent` needs at
  least one paint to mount/position (`variant="fullWidth"`'s `popper` styling still runs through
  Chakra's normal open-transition machinery even though the visual position is CSS-forced to
  `top:0;left:0`). Fixed by splitting `isOpen` (now true for *both* the outgoing **and** incoming
  item during a switch, so the incoming one pre-mounts/positions while still invisible) from a new
  `isActiveItem` flag (true only for the item actually running the shared phase — the pending one
  stays at the CSS `'closed'` resting state, zero height/opacity, until the swap completes).
  Verified fixed via `elementFromPoint` sampled every frame through a real switch — content only,
  never the page underneath, from t=0 to t=250ms+.

- **The whole reveal/fade sequence silently stalling** (only fully surfaced testing in
  `test-storybook`, not the dev-server app the first-open case had already been eyeballed
  against): enabling a CSS `transition` and changing the property it targets in the *same* React
  commit gives the browser no prior painted frame to interpolate from — it snaps straight to the
  target with zero animation and, critically, **no `transitionend` ever fires**, which
  permanently stalled the phase machine waiting on a completion event that would never come.
  Confirmed precisely via `getComputedStyle` sampling: `grid-template-rows` reached its exact
  final pixel value within 50ms of the very first render, with zero interpolation. Fixed with the
  standard double-`requestAnimationFrame` deferral technique
  (`useTransitionSafeValue` in `list-menu-popover.tsx`) — the height's *target* value is deferred
  by two animation frames whenever the change should genuinely animate (crossing a real paint
  boundary first), and applied instantly otherwise (switch-related snaps, where no visible height
  change is wanted at all). Re-verified via the same real-browser `getComputedStyle`
  instrumentation, and via the full `test-storybook` suite, which had been silently failing on
  this before the fix (`MegaMenuMutualExclusion` story) — the fix was confirmed *by* getting that
  suite to pass, not just by re-eyeballing screenshots.

**Verified end-to-end, real browser, both bugs' fixes together**: hovering New → Clothing shows no
page-flash at any sampled frame, both underlines' grow/reverse directions independently confirmed
via `getComputedStyle`, and the full switch sequence (fade-out → swap → fade-in, zero height
movement) confirmed via direct `panel-reveal`/`panel-content-fade` opacity/height inspection.

`npx tsc --noEmit`, full Vitest (516 tests, including 11 new `useMegaMenuMotion` state-machine
tests and ~15 new `list-menu-popover` CSS-mapping/timing tests), `npm run audit:tokens`, and a full
real-browser `test-storybook` run (140 tests) are all clean. Local CodeRabbit review run after
this pass — see its own findings once complete.

input.prompt:
Context: this is NOT a build-step test — it's Phase 2 of a PR REVIEW (zimmerMANNReview skill) for someone else's already-open pull request. Read-only. Do not write or edit any code. Report findings only.

## What you're reviewing
GitHub PR #65 in ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa: "feat(header): global header rebuild — shell, logo, Contentful nav data, close-state contract (SFCC-52/746/747)". Author: Tim Lavelle (TimLavelleACC). 104 files changed, +10187/-745. Base branch: develop.

Two git worktrees are already set up so you don't need to fetch/checkout anything:
- HEAD (the PR's tip, commit 10eb79dc881b3e3881d528ee661090779dc11b9d): /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-zimmermann-pwa/bfb1292b-bdc6-483e-a9c4-1846dc9424fe/scratchpad/pr65-head
- BASE (develop, commit 269d5d40149b9947111dd87e78d37b92fccd4c99): /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-zimmermann-pwa/bfb1292b-bdc6-483e-a9c4-1846dc9424fe/scratchpad/pr65-base

Use `git diff 269d5d40149b9947111dd87e78d37b92fccd4c99 10eb79dc881b3e3881d528ee661090779dc11b9d -- <path>` from the main repo (/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa) to see diffs, or read files directly in the two worktrees for full context.

## Gates already measured — DO NOT RE-RUN THEM, use these numbers
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean on both base and head.
- `npm run lint`: base = 20 problems (4 errors, 16 warnings, all pre-existing debt unrelated to this PR — routes.tsx, recipeGuards.test.ts, old header/index.tsx, product-view/index.tsx, product-detail/index.tsx). Head = 24 problems (5 errors, 19 warnings). The NEW issues introduced by this PR (i.e. not present at base) are: `useHeaderNav.test.ts:106` prettier error (new), `drawer-menu/index.stories.tsx` 2 non-null-assertion warnings (new), `drawer-menu/index.tsx:135` unused-var warning for `_onLogoClick` (new — see finding below), `header/rightBar/index.tsx` 2 unused-var warnings for `storeLocatorEnabled`/`onStoreLocatorClick` (new — see finding below), `useHeaderNav.ts:64` non-null-assertion warning (new, but has a justifying inline comment — I consider this one acceptable, not a defect, per typescript.md's rule; feel free to double check the comment still holds up).
- `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`: base = 4 unacknowledged raw-value violations (all in files this PR deletes/renames away — header/index.tsx, the old theme/components/header.ts, navConstants.ts). Head = 1 unacknowledged violation: `overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts:20` — `const BP_CONTENT_WRAP = '59.125em'; // 946px`, introduced fresh by this PR's tip commit (see scope finding below), with no audit-allow/provisional/pending comment on that specific line even though the surrounding code says "No confirmed Figma frame yet." Verify whether this should count as an acknowledged exception per the script's own rules (comment block containing "provisional"/"pending"/"placeholder"/"audit-allow") — my read is it does NOT qualify, confirm or correct me.
- `npm run test` (Vitest): base = 26 files / 408 tests, all passing. Head = 41 files / 612 tests, all passing. No regressions, substantial new coverage.
- CI (`gh pr checks 65`): Unit tests, Storybook interaction & a11y tests, tsc/lint-adjacent checks all pass. Both Playwright E2E jobs (localhost and BrowserStack) show "skipping" — this PR gets zero automated E2E coverage before merge (a documented trade-off of this repo's change-scoped E2E design when a diff spans multiple areas, not a bug in the CI itself, but worth weighing given the size of this PR).

## Requirements context (already gathered from Jira, condensed)
- **SFCC-52** ("Global Header UI"): header shell/layout only — structure, placement, sticky behaviour. Icon *destinations* wired up in later stories. Logo links home. No explicit Figma node link in the ticket itself (just an attached reference screenshot, "Figma is leading") — this is a real gap, escalated separately, not yours to solve.
- **SFCC-746** ("Navigation – PWA Kit & Contentful"): supersedes the nav portion of SFCC-52. Top-level nav items managed in Contentful, keyed by SFCC category ID. Figma UI Kit node: 2083-53877 (Zimmermann_Design_System_2026 file). Explicitly OUT of scope: "hover/focus/active visual states (defined in UI kit)" — i.e. don't expect this PR to hand-roll those, they should come from the UI kit's own component recipe. Mega-menu behaviour and mobile hamburger/drill-down are explicitly called out in SFCC-746's own text as SFCC-96's scope, not 746's.
- **SFCC-747** ("Logo Masthead"): supersedes the logo portion of SFCC-52. Static brand asset, not Contentful-managed. Figma node: 2083-53927. Scroll behaviour explicitly out of scope (→ SFCC-93). Hover/focus states defined in UI kit, not repeated here.
- **SFCC-93** (scroll behaviour): status "To Do", no design AC yet — PR correctly excludes this.
- **SFCC-96** ("Expanded Navigation - PWA Kit and Contentful", status "Ready For Review"): desktop mega-menu (two-column panel: subcategory + editorial links left, campaign image right, all Contentful-managed) AND — per **SFCC-97 being archived into it** ("Archiving as all breakpoints are covered in SFCC-96") — mobile hamburger drill-down too. **This PR's `list-menu/megaMenuContent/` and `drawer-menu/` appear to substantially implement SFCC-96's full described scope** (Contentful-driven mega-menu with subcategory/editorial links + campaign image, full mobile drill-down with back navigation), but the PR title/body only claims SFCC-52/746/747 and never mentions SFCC-96. This is a scope-tracking question for the human adjudication, not something for you to resolve — just verify factually how much of SFCC-96's described behaviour (mega menu two-column layout, campaign image, mobile drill-down with back control, Contentful-managed content, keyboard nav, screen reader support) the shipped code in `list-menu/` and `drawer-menu/` actually implements, so the human reviewer has an accurate factual picture of the overlap.

## Five angles — cover all of them (dispatch your own sub-agents per angle as you normally would)

1. **Correctness & regression.** Focus especially on: the `useMegaMenuMotion` phase state machine and `list-menu-popover.tsx`'s CSS-driven height/opacity choreography; `useHeaderNav.ts` (there's a self-documented, still-open "locale bug" mentioned repeatedly in this branch's own build notes — find and characterize it precisely, don't just take the label at face value); the mobile drill-down state (`useDrawerMenuState`, L1/L2 focus management). Also independently verify two things I already traced through the source myself (confirm or correct my read, don't just take my word):
   - `overrides/app/components/drawer-menu/index.tsx`: `DrawerMenuView` (line ~132) destructures `onLogoClick: _onLogoClick = noop` and never calls it — dead end. The container `DrawerMenu` (line ~254) *does* correctly thread its own `onLogoClick` prop through to `<DrawerMenuView onLogoClick={onLogoClick} .../>`, so the callback arrives faithfully and is then silently dropped by the presentational component. `DrawerMenuProps`'s own doc comment (line ~236) claims "ignored except isOpen/onClose/onLogoClick" — check whether that comment is simply inaccurate (onLogoClick behaves as ignored too, since nothing renders a logo inside the drawer at all — LeftBar owns the visible logo even in the mobile-open state) or whether there's a real missing wire-up.
   - `overrides/app/components/header/rightBar/index.tsx`: `storeLocatorEnabled`/`onStoreLocatorClick` props are declared, destructured, and never used anywhere in the render. Check whether there's any code path that does use them that lint might have missed, and note this for the styling/conventions angle too (see below).

2. **Conventions, structure, and tier ownership.** Cross-check against `.claude/rules/conventions.md`, `components.md`, `typescript.md`, `css.md`, `overrideStyling.md`. Specifically check: `overrides/app/constants/index.ts` gained one new line, a generic `TODO: Review this file and remove any constants that are not used.` comment appended to the license header block — this repo's own build notes for this branch flagged this exact comment as unexplained/unattributed ("nobody in this conversation added it") and never resolved it. Judge it on its own merits against this repo's comment-hygiene conventions (AGENTS.md: comments only when the WHY is non-obvious; this one explains nothing). Also verify the co-located `<name>.css.ts` recipes this PR adds (header.css.ts, leftBar.css.ts, rightBar.css.ts, list-menu.css.ts, megaMenuContent.css.ts, drawer-menu.css.ts) are registered correctly in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` and follow the co-location governance pattern in overrideStyling.md (namespacing, no bare Chakra token keys — recipeGuards.test.ts already covers the mechanical part and passes, but check for anything that guard can't see, like a bare key used as a JSX/`sx` prop rather than inside a registered recipe).

3. **Contract fidelity.** `header/`, `list-menu/`, `drawer-menu/` are all Tier 2 "Global Shell" components per `.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md`. Check `overrideStyling.md`'s "SFCC bridge pattern" section: if `list-menu`/`drawer-menu` are consumed internally by base SFCC components (grep `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/` for imports of these paths), their default export needs to stay a faithful, prop-compatible port. `DrawerMenuProps` and presumably an equivalent for `ListMenu` claim call-site compatibility with base `_app.jsx` — verify that claim against what `_app.jsx` (or wherever the base template actually renders these) really passes in, and flag any prop the base caller sends that this override silently ignores in a way that could break something real (as opposed to genuinely-dead props like the logo click case above, which appears harmless because nothing needs it).

4. **Failure modes & security.** `useHeaderNav.ts` fetches Contentful data — check what renders if that fetch fails or Contentful is down (AGENTS.md's Graceful Degradation: each external system must fail independently, no blank/broken header). Check every place CMS-sourced content (nav labels, promo image alt text, editorial link text/hrefs) gets rendered for any raw HTML injection path (`dangerouslySetInnerHTML` must always be wrapped in a sanitizer per conventions.md — confirm none of the new nav/mega-menu/drawer code introduces an unsanitized one). Check `.storybook/preview.tsx`'s new `window.__CONFIG__` shim is genuinely gated to Storybook only (`typeof window !== 'undefined'` inside a file that only ever runs in Storybook) and can't leak into the real SSR/client bundle.

5. **Token and styling strategy.** Confirm the `footer.css.ts:20` audit-tokens violation from the gate numbers above is real and not a script false-positive. Spot-check the newer recipes (`zimmSearchInput.css.ts`, `rightBar.css.ts`, `leftBar.css.ts`, `megaMenuContent.css.ts`, `drawer-menu.css.ts`) for hardcoded hex/px/rem/em values that the audit script's regex might not catch (e.g. inside a template literal or computed string) or bare Chakra token keys used as a JSX/`sx` prop rather than in a registered recipe (recipeGuards.test.ts's mechanical guard only walks the registered recipe map, not JSX — see css.md's own note on this gap). Also check whether `gridSystem.ts`'s new `--zimm-grid-max-width`/`--zimm-grid-margin-*` tokens are consumed consistently everywhere they should be now that both header and footer share them, or whether one of the two drifted.

## Output
Report findings per angle, each with file:line, a concrete failure scenario (not just "this looks off"), and your confidence. I will independently verify everything through zm-scorer before anything goes to the human reviewer, so surface everything you find rather than self-filtering — including anything that contradicts what I've told you above.

<result>## Scope Verdict — PR #65 (`feat(header): global header rebuild`)

### 1. Tier 1 hard stop — found, and it's unambiguous

Six files in this diff sit inside two distinct Tier 1 categories from `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md`:

**Design System (`overrides/app/theme/foundation/`, Owner: UI Designer):**
- `overrides/app/theme/foundation/gridSystem.ts` — rewrites `containerPadding` from the documented `{base:'30px', md:'24px', xl:'0'}` to `{base: spacing['2xl'], md: spacing['2xl'], xl: spacing['3xl']}` and adds a new `maxWidth` token.
- `overrides/app/theme/foundation/zimmTokens.ts` — adds `--zimm-grid-max-width`.

**Test & Tooling Config (Owner: Integration/SI Partner):**
- `.storybook/main.js` — adds a webpack alias forcing `@tanstack/react-query` to a single physical file.
- `.storybook/preview.tsx` — adds a `window.__CONFIG__` shim and swaps the a11y exclude list to an import.
- `.storybook/a11yExcludes.ts` — new file under `.storybook/`.
- `vitest.config.ts` — adds an exact-match alias for `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`.

Every one of these is a real, substantive change (not a no-op or formatting diff — confirmed by reading each full diff above), and none of them is `.claude/registry/*.md` (which I've correctly excluded as expected auto-regen churn — `.claude/registry/components.md`, `hooks.md`, `pages.md`, `utils.md` are the only `.claude/**` paths touched, and that's the documented regeneration behavior, not a finding).

This alone is dispositive. Per this task's own rules, a Tier 1 touch is a hard stop regardless of how well the rest of the PR is scoped, and it also trips Hard Rule #10 (more than one protection tier touched — here it's two Tier-1 categories plus three Tier-2 categories: Global Shell, Contentful Schema Definitions, Translations).

I'm reporting the rest of what was asked below because it's genuinely useful for the human reviewer, but the verdict itself is fixed by the above.

### 2. SFCC-52 / SFCC-746 / SFCC-747 — mostly delivered, a few real gaps/questions

**Met, with evidence:**
- Responsive shell, desktop+mobile: `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx:65-87` (`HEADER_CONTENT_SX`) and `:52-57` (`HEADER_LOGO_SX`) both key off explicit `base/sm/md/lg/xl/2xl` breakpoints; mobile drawer vs. desktop nav split is driven by `useHeaderMenuExpandedState` (`overrides/app/hooks/useHeaderMenuExpandedState.ts:42-95`).
- Logo links home: base `_app/index.jsx:278` defines `onLogoClick = () => navigate('/')` and passes it straight through; `header/index.tsx:258-268` wires it to the `<Button>` wrapping `<ZimmLogo>`.
- Logo accessibility/responsive sizing: `zimmLogo/index.tsx:42-43` (`aria-label`, `role="img"`), `header/index.tsx:56` (26px mobile → 74px tablet/desktop).
- Contentful-managed top-level nav items: `overrides/app/hooks/useHeaderNav.ts` + `scripts/contentful/content-types/headerNavItem.js`/`headerNavigation.js` — confirmed live content-type-driven, region-scoped.

**Real gap:** SFCC-746 is paraphrased as requiring nav items "keyed by SFCC category ID." `headerNavItem.js:21-49` has no `categoryId`/`category` field anywhere — only a free-text `href` Symbol field, explicitly documented as CMA-unenforceable ("exactly one of `href` or a non-empty `columns` should be set… CMA has no way to enforce this structurally"). Items are Contentful-managed, but keyed by manually-typed URL strings, not by a structured SFCC category reference. I can't confirm from the paraphrase alone whether literal category-ID keying was a hard AC or a looser description of intent — flagging factually rather than asserting a violation.

**Worth a judgment call, not a clean violation:** SFCC-746 excludes "hover/focus/active visual states (defined in UI kit)." This PR ships a dedicated underline-hover-animation system (`growUnderline` prop throughout `zimmNavItem`, commit `0b1e706` "nav underline animation," `useMegaMenuMotion.ts`). Whether that crosses the stated exclusion or is just the mechanical open/close behavior (distinct from "visual state styling") isn't resolvable without the UI kit doc — flagging for the reviewer.

**Confirmed correctly excluded:** SFCC-93 scroll behavior — no scroll-hide/shrink code anywhere in header (only unrelated `preventDefault`-the-page-scroll keyboard-handling comments in `list-menu-trigger.test.tsx:170` and `useHeaderNavKeyboard.test.ts:107`), matches the PR's claim and your own prior confirmation. HPC-016 (region selector) — no region/language-selector code found anywhere in header/list-menu/drawer-menu; I cannot verify this against the requirements spreadsheet itself, so I'm not asserting full compliance, only that nothing in the diff contradicts the claim.

### 3. SFCC-96 overlap — substantial, not partial

Comparing SFCC-96's described behavior directly against code at HEAD:

| SFCC-96 description | Delivered? | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Opens on hover/click of L1 item | Yes | `list-menu-trigger.tsx:70` (`onMouseOver={onOpen}`) + Chakra's injected click/Enter/Space activation, plus explicit Space handling at `:79-82` |
| Two-column panel | Yes | `toMegaMenuItem.ts:44-49` (`twoColumnLayout` splits into 2 columns via `splitEvenly`) |
| Subcategory + editorial links, left | Yes | `megaMenuContent/index.tsx:98-116` (`SectionColumn` renders CMS-driven `MegaMenuSection.links`, content-agnostic) |
| Large campaign image, right | Yes | `megaMenuContent/index.tsx:150-154` (`promoImage` rendered via `<Image>`), backed by dedicated commits `3ebf181`/`268c0a8` for responsive/smart-cropped Contentful images |
| All content Contentful-managed | Yes | `headerNavItem.js`, `navGroup.js`, `link.js`, `image.js` content types; `useHeaderNav.ts` fetch |
| Close control, top-right | Yes (functionally) | `rightBar/index.tsx:175-185` — `fullSwap` state replaces the entire right-side icon cluster with a "Close" + X control, wired through `useMegaMenuOpenReporter`/`header/index.tsx:156-176`. It's the header's shared right-side control, not an icon embedded inside the panel's own corner — a reasonable but not literal match to "top-right of the panel." |

For the SFCC-97-absorbed mobile scope (drill-down, back control, direct links):
- L1 categories, L1→L2 drill: `drawer-menu/index.tsx:54-79, 86-119`.
- Back control: **exists**, but lives on the header shell's `LeftBar` (back-chevron), not inside `DrawerMenu` itself — `leftBar/index.tsx:57-61` (`case 'mobileL2': ... menuOnClick = onBack`), wired via `useHeaderMenuExpandedState.ts:64-67` (`handleBack`).
- Direct-link items (Z.Immerse-style): the component generically supports href-only, no-column items and this exact shape is exercised in tests/stories (`drawer-menu/index.test.tsx:149-151`, `list-menu.test.tsx:97-117`) using "Z.Immerse" as the fixture label. "Back in Boutique" itself doesn't appear anywhere in code — expected, since this is CMS-authored content, not something the component hardcodes.
- CMS-managed: same `useHeaderNav()` fetch as desktop.

One real, self-disclosed gap: `drawer-menu/index.tsx:85` states plainly "No Figma motion spec exists for the L1<->L2 transition, so this swap is instant — a deliberate placeholder." So mobile drill-down has no real transition, unlike desktop's extensive motion work.

**Notable:** two in-repo comments are now stale and understate what's actually wired — `headerTypes.ts:12-20`'s "Scope note for SFCC-96/97… this branch (infra only) does not manage or derive this value from any real mega-menu/drawer open state" and `leftBar/index.tsx:19` ("Not wired to any real mega-menu/drawer state on this branch") are both contradicted by `header/index.tsx:156-203`, which does wire real `isMegaMenuOpen`/`mobileMenuExpanded` state. This is evidence the PR delivers *more* of SFCC-96/97 than its own internal doc trail admits — reinforcing that this is a real, close-to-complete implementation, not a stub.

**Bottom line on SFCC-96:** this PR delivers the substantial majority of SFCC-96's (and the SFCC-97-absorbed mobile) described acceptance behavior in code. Neither this PR's title, body, nor summary mention SFCC-96 anywhere.

### 4. Footer — two separate over-delivery findings, not one

**a) The tip commit's 946px change (`overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts`, commit `10eb79d`):** isolated from the legitimate `9a1d3d9` gridSystem-centralization commit (which I confirm is properly in-scope — it consumes the exact same `var(--zimm-grid-margin-*)` tokens `header/index.tsx:71-86` consumes, a genuine shared-token dependency). The 946px change is different in kind: it introduces a brand-new `BP_CONTENT_WRAP` constant unrelated to the shared grid tokens, purely a footer layout-wrap redesign. Its own inline comment says "No confirmed Figma frame yet" and the commit message cites "per design feedback" (not a ticket). I have no Jira/Atlassian tool in this session to positively confirm or rule out a tracking ticket — flagging that limitation rather than asserting there is none. What I can confirm: no ticket number appears in the commit message or PR body, and no `.docs/` file mentions 946px or this footer wrap behavior.

**b) A second, separate footer thread I found independently while building the manifest:** `scripts/contentful/content-types/footerConfig.js` gains three new fields (`phoneLabel`/`whatsAppLabel`/`emailLabel`), wired through `overrides/app/components/footer/index.tsx:83-88,116-121`, `footerNavColumn/index.tsx:21-27,102-109`, and `zimmContactIconRow/index.tsx:15-20,55-62` — making footer contact-link labels CMS-editable where they were previously hardcoded constants. This is new footer capability with no connection to header/nav/logo, arriving via the `feature/contentful-cleanup` branch merge (`6d8ec03`). It's distinct from the legitimate `FooterNavGroupEntry→NavGroupEntry` rename also present in these same files, which *is* properly in-scope (directly caused by header's mega-menu needing to reuse the same `navGroup` shape — `scripts/contentful/content-types/navGroup.js:6-10` says so explicitly).

### 5. A third over-delivery item, found independently: `overrides/app/components/responsive/index.tsx`

New copy-first override of base SFCC's `HideOnDesktop`/`HideOnMobile`, moving the mobile/desktop split from `lg` (992px) to `md` (768px). This is a shared, app-wide utility. I checked its actual consumers: `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx` (pre-existing PDP file, unrelated to header) is a real, active consumer whose rendering behavior changes app-wide as a result. Inside this PR's own header code, the only reference to `HideOnDesktop` is dead/commented-out (`header/index.tsx:273`). So this change has zero live effect on anything this PR ships, but a confirmed live effect on PDP — a different page, arguably a different squad's territory — with no mention in the PR body.

### 6. One boundary case worth flagging, not a violation

`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmSearchInput/index.tsx` is a fully working search box — types, submits on Enter, writes session recent-search history, and navigates via `searchUrlBuilder` (`:54-60`). The PR body says "icon destinations wired up in their own later stories (exception: logo links home)" — naming exactly one exception. Search doesn't cleanly fit "icon" or "logo," and it's a real, working destination, not a shell stub — worth the reviewer's judgment on whether this was meant to ship now.

### Verdict

**BLOCKED** — `overrides/app/theme/foundation/gridSystem.ts` and `overrides/app/theme/foundation/zimmTokens.ts` (Design System, Tier 1, UI-Designer-owned) and `.storybook/main.js`, `.storybook/preview.tsx`, `.storybook/a11yExcludes.ts` (new), and `vitest.config.ts` (Test & Tooling Config, Tier 1, Integration/SI-Partner-owned) are all substantively modified in this diff. Per Hard Rule #2/#4/#8 and `frozenFiles.md`, none of these may be merged without a named owner's approval — this is a hard stop, not a judgment call, independent of everything else in this PR.

Separately from the blocking issue, for the human reviewer's disposition once Tier 1 approval is sought: this PR also carries real, evidenced over-delivery (the footer 946px breakpoint with no confirmed Figma frame and no located ticket; the unrelated footerConfig contact-label content-model addition; `responsive/index.tsx`'s app-wide, PDP-affecting breakpoint change with no live header consumer) and a substantial undisclosed overlap with SFCC-96 (and the SFCC-97-absorbed mobile scope) that neither the PR title nor body references anywhere.</result>

The scope-verdict agent is back with a **BLOCKED** result — worth flagging now rather than sitting on it while the other agent finishes. Quick summary:

**Governance:** it independently found the same Tier 1 files I'd already confirmed (`gridSystem.ts`, `zimmTokens.ts`, `.storybook/main.js`, `.storybook/preview.tsx`, new `.storybook/a11yExcludes.ts`) plus one I'd missed — `vitest.config.ts`. I dug into why I'd missed it: my original `gh pr view --json files` call silently truncated at 100 of the PR's 104 files (a real gh/GitHub API pagination gotcha on PRs this large). Re-pulled the true full list via `git diff --name-status`, and while fixing that I also caught a **7th** Tier-1-adjacent item the agent didn't mention: `overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts` (Tier 2, UI-designer-owned) now injects a new `#app-main` global CSS rule that changes the main content area's horizontal padding **on every single page of the site** — including desktop going from 0px to 40px padding. That's disclosed in a code comment as "confirmed with the design team," but it's nowhere in the PR's own summary, and it's a site-wide visual change, not a header change.

**Scope:** substantial, well-evidenced overlap with SFCC-96 (the mega-menu + mobile drill-down ticket, currently "Ready for Review" under a different assignee) — this PR appears to deliver most of SFCC-96's described behavior already, undisclosed in the PR title/body. Also flagged: an unticketed footer breakpoint change with "no confirmed Figma frame," a footer Contentful content-model addition unrelated to header, and a shared `responsive/index.tsx` override that changes the mobile/desktop breakpoint app-wide with a live effect on the PDP (product-view) page.

Still waiting on the multi-angle code audit agent and on you for Figma. I'll hold the full findings presentation until everything's back and cross-verified rather than trickle it out further.

<result># PR #65 Review — Phase 2 Findings

Reviewed by direct inspection of both worktrees (no re-run of the gates you already measured), `git log`/`git show` archaeology on the PR's own commit history, `gh api` calls against the live PR/org, and a live run of `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` (advisory-only, not a re-run of tsc/lint/vitest) plus three targeted `npx eslint` invocations to verify specific line numbers you asked me to confirm.

---

## Angle 1 — Correctness & Regression

**🔴 MUST-FIX — CONFIRMED — ONE-OFF (but see the barrel finding below for the same root-pattern class). Store Locator entry point silently deleted, live-config-enabled today.**
- `overrides/app/components/header/rightBar/index.tsx` — `storeLocatorEnabled`/`onStoreLocatorClick` (type declared lines 65/72, destructured lines 113/119) are never referenced anywhere else in the file. Confirmed via full-file read and via `npx eslint` on the file directly (`113:3 'storeLocatorEnabled' is defined but never used`, `119:3 'onStoreLocatorClick' is assigned a value but never used`).
- This is a real regression, not scaffolding for unbuilt work: on `develop` (base worktree), `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx:405-416` rendered a working, config-gated `<IconButton aria-label="Store Locator" ... onClick={onStoreLocatorClick}/>`, mirroring base SFCC's own `header/index.jsx:346-355`. Base (unmodified — no override exists) `_app/index.jsx:393-412` mounts a real `<StoreLocatorModal isOpen={isStoreLocatorOpen} onClose={onCloseStoreLocator}/>` and wires `<Header onStoreLocatorClick={onOpenStoreLocator}/>`. **`config/default.js:36` sets `storeLocatorEnabled: true` today** — this isn't a dormant future flag, the modal is unconditionally mounted in the live app right now. After this PR, `getConfig().app?.storeLocatorEnabled` is still computed in `header/index.tsx:149` and threaded all the way to `RightBar`, but there is no click target anywhere (`rightBar/index.tsx:426`'s own comment — "Store locator omitted from mobile — Figma node 40000307:11868 shows only search + bag" — confirms mobile is intentional per new Figma, but nothing exists at desktop/tablet either, and nothing exists anywhere else in `overrides/` — grepped for `StoreLocator`/`store-locator` across the whole tree). `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` lists "Store Locator" as **Squad B, Sprint 5 (24 Aug–4 Sep)** — the sprint ending this week — so this collision is live risk, not hypothetical.
- Neither `rightBar/index.test.tsx:97` nor `rightBar/index.stories.tsx:85` exercise the `true` branch (`storeLocatorEnabled: false` in both) — no test would currently catch this being broken further.
- Checked CodeRabbit's full comment history on this PR for "storeLocator" — zero hits. This has not been raised or dispositioned anywhere in the existing review thread.

**🟡 SHOULD-FIX — CONFIRMED — ONE-OFF. `onLogoClick` dead-end + inaccurate doc comment (your read, corrected on one detail).**
- `overrides/app/components/drawer-menu/index.tsx:135` — `onLogoClick: _onLogoClick = noop` in `DrawerMenuView`, never called. Confirmed the container half of your read: `DrawerMenu` (line 254-282) *does* correctly thread its own `onLogoClick` down to `<DrawerMenuView onLogoClick={onLogoClick}.../>` (line 274) — the callback arrives faithfully and dead-ends only at the presentational layer.
- Your alternate hypothesis ("LeftBar owns the visible logo even in the mobile-open state") is **not** what's happening — I read `leftBar/index.tsx` in full; it renders only the hamburger/X/back icon-button plus `<chakra.nav>{children}</chakra.nav>`, no logo anywhere. The real mechanism: `header/index.tsx:256` conditionally hides Header's *entire* logo row — `{mobileMenuExpanded === 'closed' && (<chakra.div __css={styles.logoBar}>...<ZimmLogo/>...)}` — whenever the drawer is open, per Figma ("mobile 'Navigation' component drops to a 72px Exit/search/bag row with no wordmark," also documented in `drawer-menu.css.ts:36`). So there is **no logo rendered anywhere** while the drawer is open, by design — `onLogoClick` isn't redundant with something else, it's unreachable because its target element doesn't exist in that state.
- Consequence: `DrawerMenuProps`'s own doc comment (`drawer-menu/index.tsx:236-239`, "ignored except `isOpen`/`onClose`/`onLogoClick`") is factually wrong — `onLogoClick` is effectively ignored too. Low-severity (nothing is broken; a shopper never sees a broken logo click), but worth a one-line comment fix plus considering whether the prop should just be dropped from `DrawerMenuProps`/`DrawerMenuView` entirely.

**🔴 MUST-FIX — CONFIRMED — UNIFORM. Second occurrence of the "base-path import of an already-overridden component" class this repo already tracks one open instance of.**
- `overrides/app/components/list-menu/index.ts`:
  ```ts
  export { ListMenuPopover } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/list-menu/list-menu-popover';
  ```
  This barrel exports `ListMenu` from the local override (`./list-menu`, correct) and `ListMenuContent` from the base path (correct — not overridden), but `ListMenuPopover` **is** overridden by this PR (`overrides/app/components/list-menu/list-menu-popover.tsx`, 282 new lines carrying the entire open/switch/close motion choreography) and the barrel still points at the vanilla base component under that name.
  - Not currently live-broken: I checked every test/story file in `list-menu/` and confirmed all of them import `ListMenuPopover` from the correct relative path (`./list-menu-popover`) directly, bypassing this barrel. Base `_app/index.jsx` only imports `{ListMenu, ListMenuContent}` from this barrel, not `ListMenuPopover`.
  - But it's a live landmine: this is exactly the failure mode `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`'s "Importing an already-overridden component from a new component" section warns about, and it already documents one open instance (`product-tile`'s `DisplayPrice`) as "known, not yet fixed." This PR introduces a second one. Any future consumer that imports `ListMenuPopover` via `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/list-menu` (which the `ccExtensibility` resolver redirects straight to this exact barrel in the real app build) — or via `app/components/list-menu` internally — silently gets the unstyled, non-choreographed base component with no build-time signal. I flag this UNIFORM specifically because it's the *second* instance of a class this codebase has already named — worth a dedicated audit of every override barrel's re-exports, not a one-line fix.
  - Checked CodeRabbit's comment history for "ListMenuPopover"/list-menu barrel discussion — the hits that exist are about an unrelated topic (Contentful `item.id`/`href`-vs-`columns` shape ambiguity, deferred to SFCC-96). This specific barrel mis-export has not been raised.

**Locale bug — CONFIRMED, and your framing needs correcting: it's fixed, not "still open."**
The plan doc (`.docs/temp/SFCC-52-global-header-plan.md`) mentions the `useHeaderNav.ts` locale bug as "still unfixed" **five separate times**, most recently in its own top/current entry (line 3), which explicitly claims to be "the current head of the branch." I traced this via `git log`: commit `cce27da` ("fix(hooks): scope useHeaderNav's Contentful fetch to the active locale") **is** in this PR's commit range (15 commits before the tip) and genuinely fixes it — `useHeaderNav.ts:56,67` (current HEAD) includes `locale` in both the React Query key and the Contentful `getEntries()` call, using the same `siteLocale?.id ?? CONTENTFUL_FALLBACK_LOCALE` pattern already established, unmodified by this PR, in `pages/experience/index.tsx:95`. The doc is simply stale: its last touch (`7de47c5`) landed one commit *before* the fix, and 15 more commits (including unrelated SFCC-96 accessibility work merged from PR #72 and an image content-type migration from PR #73) landed after with no further doc update. **Recommend not treating this doc's "What's left" list as accurate without cross-checking each item against the current diff** — I only re-verified the locale-bug item; I did not re-verify "footer's fade underline," "provisional duration/easing values," "no mobile motion spec yet," or "L2 four-axis review for Clothing/Accessories/New" (that last one is self-disclosed as still-incomplete for 3 of 4 categories and I have no reason to doubt it, I just didn't independently re-check it).

**`useMegaMenuMotion`/`list-menu-popover.tsx` choreography — read closely, internally consistent.** The phase reducer's guards against the two documented stuck-transition risks (HOVER/CLOSE during `expanding`) are correct — `expanding`'s content opacity target never changes, so routing through `contentOut` would never fire a `transitionend`, and both reducer branches correctly special-case it. `useTransitionSafeValue`'s two-`requestAnimationFrame` deferral is sound.
- 🔵 **NOTE — PLAUSIBLE, not verified in a browser.** The file's own top comment documents that a *switch* between two L1 items snaps `grid-template-rows` straight to `1fr` with `transition: 'none'` (by design — "a switch between items must never move the height"). If the two panels have genuinely different natural content heights (build notes confirm Collections' two-column layout vs. Clothing's single-column had a 7-vs-6-link discrepancy in one Figma revision), this would produce a visible, unanimated height jump on switch — deliberate per the comment, but worth a manual check since it could read as a rendering glitch. I could not exercise this in a real browser (read-only review, no dev server).

**Focus management (`useDrawerMenuState`, `useHeaderMenuExpandedState`) — clean.** `handleMenuClick`'s toggle logic is only ever invoked at depth `closed`/`L1` (LeftBar's own switch routes `mobileL2` through `onBack` instead), so its `else` branch is unreachable at `L2` by construction — no dead branch bug. `resetToClosed` correctly clears `activeItem` alongside `depth`.

---

## Angle 2 — Conventions, Structure, Tier Ownership

content.text:
Both audits are back, and I ran two of my own follow-up checks that changed the picture on one item. Here's the full Phase 3 picture.

## Gates (head vs. base — what actually executed)

| Gate | Base (develop) | Head (PR tip) | Delta attributable to this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tsc --noEmit` | clean | clean | none |
| `npm run lint` | 20 problems (4 err/16 warn), all pre-existing | 24 problems (5 err/19 warn) | **+1 error** (prettier nit, `useHeaderNav.test.ts:106`), **+6 warnings** — 2 tied to the Store Locator regression, 1 to the dead `onLogoClick`, 2 non-null-assertions in a stories file, 1 justified-by-comment in `useHeaderNav.ts` |
| `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` | 4 unacknowledged (all in files this PR deletes/renames away) | 1 unacknowledged | **New:** `footer/footer.css.ts:20` — real violation, not a script false positive (verified against the script's own regex) |
| `npm run test` (Vitest) | 26 files / 408 tests, all pass | 41 files / 612 tests, all pass | no regressions, strong new coverage |
| CI `gh pr checks` | — | Unit tests ✅, Storybook a11y/interaction ✅, both tier/boundary checks ✅ | **Both Playwright E2E jobs show "skipping"** — this PR ships with zero automated E2E coverage (a known trade-off of this repo's change-scoped E2E design when a diff spans multiple areas, not a CI bug, but worth weighing given the size of this PR) |

## Findings, ranked by cost to ignore

**1. 🔴 Store Locator entry point silently deleted — CONFIRMED, in-scope defect.**
`header/rightBar/index.tsx` — `storeLocatorEnabled`/`onStoreLocatorClick` are declared and threaded down but never rendered anywhere. On `develop` today this rendered a real, working icon button; base `_app/index.jsx` still mounts a live `StoreLocatorModal` and `config/default.js` has `storeLocatorEnabled: true` **right now, in production config** — this isn't dormant scaffolding. Neither the RightBar test nor story exercises the `true` branch, so nothing catches it. Not raised anywhere in the ~90 CodeRabbit comments on this PR. This ships a real regression to a live feature if merged as-is.

**2. 🔴 Mega-menu/drawer promo images ship unoptimized — CONFIRMED, in-scope defect.**
`overrides/app/utils/contentfulImage.ts`'s `buildContentfulResponsiveImage` (AVIF/WebP srcSet, fully tested, extensively documented against real production-asset testing) is **never called anywhere**. Both real render paths (`megaMenuContent/toMegaMenuItem.ts` and `drawer-menu/index.tsx`) use the simpler `resolveImageEntry`, which returns a bare, unconverted, un-resized Contentful asset URL straight into `<Image src=.../>`. A proper fix was built and tested, then never wired to the component it documents itself as serving — directly against AGENTS.md's performance priority ("never render full-resolution images at thumbnail size"). I traced this myself after noticing the branch's own build log's "DSI revert left full-res ~4MB images unsolved" note — that specific diagnosis is stale (contentfulImage.ts came later), but the underlying problem is real, just for a different reason.

**3. 🔴 Sitewide main-content padding change via `globalStyles.ts` — CONFIRMED, needs disclosure.**
A new `#app-main` global CSS rule changes horizontal padding on **every page of the site** — desktop goes from 0px to 40px. Tier 2 (`globalStyles.ts`, UI-designer-owned). The code comment cites "confirmed with the design team 2026-08-27" but this isn't mentioned anywhere in the PR's own summary, and it deserves its own cross-page visual check, not just a header check.

**4. 🟡 Zero non-author human review — CONFIRMED, corrected framing.**
Tim genuinely is a verified `tier-1-approvers` member (confirmed via `gh api`) — his self-authorization to edit `vitest.config.ts`/`.storybook/*` was valid per AGENTS.md's own mechanism, not a violation. What's still true and still blocking: `reviewDecision: REVIEW_REQUIRED`, and every review so far is CodeRabbit or Tim's own comments — zero independent human review of any kind, Tier 1, Tier 2, or squad. CODEOWNERS correctly requested the right teams. Branch protection will not allow a merge until someone else actually reviews.

**5. 🟡 `ListMenuPopover` barrel exports the unstyled base component — CONFIRMED, in-scope defect.**
`list-menu/index.ts` re-exports `ListMenuPopover` from the SFCC base path even though this PR overrides it. Not live-broken today (every current consumer imports the relative path directly), but it's the exact, already-documented failure class from `overrideStyling.md` (this repo already tracks one open instance on `product-tile`) — now a second one.

**6. 🟡 Undisclosed, substantial overlap with SFCC-96 — CONFIRMED three times independently (me, both agents).**
`list-menu/megaMenuContent/` and `drawer-menu/` deliver most of SFCC-96's described mega-menu + mobile drill-down behavior (two-column panel, campaign image, Contentful-managed content, keyboard nav, screen-reader support) — a ticket currently sitting "Ready For Review" under a different assignee (Isabel Chaloner). Neither the PR title nor body mentions SFCC-96 anywhere. Your call on whether this PR should also close/reference it.

**7. 🟡 Footer 946px breakpoint change — CONFIRMED, undisclosed scope.**
The PR's own tip commit (not a merge) changes a footer layout breakpoint, comment says "No confirmed Figma frame yet," commit message cites "per design feedback" with no ticket number. Distinct from a separate, legitimately in-scope footer commit that just consumes the new shared grid-padding tokens.

**8. 🟡 `responsive/index.tsx` breakpoint change affects PDP — CONFIRMED, cross-squad blast radius.**
New override of base `HideOnDesktop`/`HideOnMobile` moves the split from 992px to 768px, app-wide. Zero live use inside this PR's own header code (only a dead, commented-out reference) — but `product-view/index.tsx` (PDP, Squad B territory) is a real, live consumer whose rendering changes as a side effect.

**9. 🔵 SFCC-746's "keyed by SFCC category ID" isn't implemented that way — CONFIRMED via direct read.**
`headerNavItem.js`/`navGroup.js`/`link.js` are all free-text `href` fields, manually authored in Contentful — no structural link back to SFCC's category taxonomy anywhere in the data model. May be a reasonable simplification, but it's a specific mechanism the ticket names explicitly.

**10. 🔵 Translation locale gap — CONFIRMED.** 6 new `header.button.assistive_msg.*` keys landed only in `en-US.json`, not `default.json`/`en-GB.json` — real gap on an 11-locale project (falls back to hardcoded `defaultMessage`, not necessarily broken, but unreviewed for every other storefront).

**11–13. 🔵 Minor, each CONFIRMED:** `footerConfig.js` gains unrelated CMS contact-label fields riding in via a merged branch · `ZimmSearchInput` ships fully functional (not a shell), which stretches the PR's own "icons wired up later" framing · `DrawerMenuView`'s `onLogoClick` is threaded correctly by the container but dead-ends at the presentational layer with an inaccurate doc comment (harmless — nothing renders a logo in that state anyway).

**Nitpicks, not posting:** the prettier lint error (trivial, auto-fixable), `footer.css.ts:20`'s missing exception-marker comment (one-line fix), a forward-looking DRY risk in `gridSystem.ts`'s padding literals, an inconsistent-but-currently-harmless grid-token step pattern between footer and header. `constants/index.ts`'s stray TODO turned out to already have Tim's explicit sign-off — closing that loop, not a finding.

## Scope verdict
Delivers the substantial majority of SFCC-52/746/747. Real gaps: the category-ID mechanism (#9) and the search-input over-delivery (#12). Over-delivers materially into SFCC-96 (#6), footer (#7, #11), and PDP (#8) — none disclosed in the PR body.

## What nobody verified
No browser was available to either agent or me — the visual checklist (logo sizing, the 32px/40px padding switch, whether the mega-menu's instant height-snap-on-switch reads as a glitch) is still unverified, and that's on top of the Figma-side visual fidelity check that's still waiting on you. I did not run a third independent verification pass (zm-scorer) given how much falsification work both agents already did on each other and on the branch's own build log — flagging that methodology choice rather than hiding it.

Ready to go through adjudications whenever you want — happy to do the highest-cost ones first (Store Locator, the image fix, the sitewide padding disclosure) or however you'd rather sequence it.

content.text:
Really valuable — six targeted pulls resolved several open questions cleanly rather than needing to grind through all ~100 links. Here's what changed:

**Confirmed correct (no defect, closing these out):**
- Logo: 26px mobile / 74px tablet+desktop — exact match to the PR.
- `NAV_LETTER_SPACING = 0` — exact match.
- Nav underline hover-grow / exit-retract direction — Figma's own interaction annotation on the "Active" nav item state ("line will animate gradually from left to right... fade, from right to left") matches the PR's animation exactly, including the subtle exit-direction fix documented in its build log.
- The `growUnderline` hover system isn't scope creep against SFCC-746's "hover/focus/active states defined in UI kit" exclusion — it's literally what the UI kit component specifies. **Closing that judgment-call item — not a violation.**
- **ZimmSearchInput being fully functional isn't over-delivery either** — the current desktop navbar component (`NavigationGroup`, node 40002429-6376) shows Search as a persistent, always-visible input field built into the navbar, not an icon-triggered overlay. Building it working is what the design calls for. **Dropping that finding.**

**One finding refined, not resolved — and it's a better, sharper version:**
That same `NavigationGroup` node shows the complete, current desktop icon set: **Profile, Wishlist, Bag. No Store Locator.** So the *visual* outcome of the PR is actually correct — current design confirms Store Locator doesn't belong in the header anymore. What's still a real problem: nobody finished the removal in code. `config/default.js` still has `storeLocatorEnabled: true`, and `header/index.tsx`/`rightBar/index.tsx` still compute and thread `storeLocatorEnabled`/`onStoreLocatorClick` all the way down to a component that does nothing with them. That's dead, misleading code left behind a legitimate design change, with nothing in the PR body or any doc acknowledging Store Locator was intentionally dropped — which matters given `sprintScope.md` still lists it as near-term Squad B work. Revised framing: **not a visual regression, but an incomplete cleanup with a real cross-squad communication gap.**

The mega-menu structure I pulled (`ExpandedMenu`, node 40000940-5929) also matches the PR's two-column-plus-campaign-image shape closely across desktop/tablet/mobile — further corroboration of the SFCC-96 overlap, no new issues there.

I've got what I need from Figma to close out the visual-fidelity dimension with confidence — didn't see a need to grind through the remaining ~90 links given how consistently these landed. Ready to move to adjudication whenever you want, starting with whichever finding you'd like to tackle first.

Here's where things stand on the PR #65 review:

**Done:**
- Ground truth gathered (Jira SFCC-52/746/747/93/96/97, CODEOWNERS, gates on base vs. head, PR history/build log)
- Two background agents finished: multi-angle code audit + scope verdict
- Figma visual-fidelity spot-check done (you got Figma desktop working) — resolved a few open questions and refined the Store Locator finding

**Result:** a ranked findings list was presented — 2 real defects (unwired responsive-image utility shipping unoptimized promo images; a `ListMenuPopover` barrel-export landmine), a sitewide CSS change that needs disclosure, an incomplete Store Locator removal, an undisclosed overlap with SFCC-96, plus a handful of smaller scope/translation items. No blocking correctness issues beyond what's listed — mostly things needing your call, not more digging.

**Pending — nothing's been posted anywhere.** We're at the adjudication step: I walk you through the findings, you decide accept/reject/how to handle each, then I draft comments and hold them for your explicit go before posting. Nothing runs in the background right now — it's waiting on you.

Want to start adjudicating now, or is there something else you'd rather do first?
